Build under test = B0: a NEW frozen snapshot (scripts/perf-worker/hb-mksnap.sh <name>, then replace its pkg symlink by a real copy of a RELEASE pkg/) of the MERGED round-3 phase-A tree (the round-2 fixes included). It must carry the readers of occlusionCull=rigs, rigPoseSkip, skipEmptyPasses, animSceneryBatch and bakeFallbackWaves (`b0Snapshot` below; uploadWarmDraw's reader is no longer required: the flag was deleted 2026-10-30 after D1), checked in M1-PRE by `hbbench.mjs --check-snapshot` against the snapshot's OWN code files, never only url-flags.md: hb-mksnap.sh symlinks docs/ into the live tree, so the url-flags.md a snapshot shows always reads current. Served with `python3 scripts/serve.py --bind 127.0.0.1 --port 8766 --check` from the snapshot. On B0 `rustParticles` is default OFF (16 scene-core flags on): an empty-flag arm is the 16-on config, and any arm that depends on another flag value names it.

Harness v2 protocol (plan section 4), all applied by hbbench.mjs / hbanatomy.mjs unless an arm overrides it: skytime=13 and DayGroup 0 ('Sunny', applied through setGameDayOverride(39, 10)); adaptiveRes=off, targetFps=0, renderScale=1, and gpuGovernor=off once R3-11's flag has a url-flags.md row (hbbench detects it); 1920x1080 INNER window unless the arm says 1280,720; interleaved, rotated order; the 65 s login cool-down; box samples (hbwho.ps1 + top processes by CPU) before, between and after segments. `--compat v1` is ONLY for RC-BENCH v2 reps 2-3 on the rep-1 snapshot (batch-RC-rust-scene-core-2026-10-26.json), never for these items: it keeps the pre-v2 step sequence exactly, so its box samples run only before launch and after the tour (hbreport also reads the bench dir's boxwatch.log for the samples in between).

The attach modes (`hbsweep.mjs` / `hbanatomy.mjs --attach`) are for the laptop tab check and ad-hoc looks; they apply DayGroup 0 and record every pin problem (`session.problems`).
Run without the gate override (gate-owner-ok.txt) whenever possible so hbgate.ps1's idle rule applies; rule V below decides validity from the run JSON either way.

decisionRules.name: validity
decisionRules.text: An arm-rep is INVALID, re-queued and never averaged, if any of these hold: `idle` < 60 s in any boxwatch sample; `gpu3d_other` > 5%; any non-test process using >= 1 CPU core-equivalent in any sample [D threshold; the bench-1 Seagate Toolkit case]; entity count differs from arm A by > 10% (R3-0 server-state pin) [D threshold]; console errors > 0; dev wasm; wrong adapter. If two scheduled windows yield no valid reps for an arm, accept 5 reps with a reported A/A noise in place of the idle gate, and mark the result "noisy box".
decisionRules.implementation: hbreport.py rule_v / assess (`--noisy-box` for the fallback); the >= 1 core test reads >= 0.95 core-equivalents over the ~2 s sample window; a rep overlapping a boxEvents cpu-hog entry is CONTAMINATED; a rep with no box sample at all is INVALID (unverified).

decisionRules.name: noise
decisionRules.text: noise = max(|A - A'|, half of A's rep spread). A delta is real only if it exceeds max(2 x noise, 3% fps or 0.5 ms).
decisionRules.implementation: hbreport.py noise_of / compare (frame-count metrics use a floor of 1).

decisionRules.name: scoring
decisionRules.text: Score on the binding thread's ms (main busy per frame, CrGpuMain WEBGL per present, GPU ms), plus still / moving / tour fps, p50 / p95, h100 / h250 / max / jank. Never on draw counts alone; draw counts are heading-binned and reported with multidraw ranges.

decisionRules.name: keep
decisionRules.text: A perf change goes or stays default-on only if all five hold: (i) its binding-thread ms moved by >= 50% of the prediction; (ii) at least one of still / moving / tour fps improved by a real delta, and no segment regressed by one; (iii) hitch metrics not worse by a real delta; (iv) 0 console errors; (v) the look gate (R4) passed. Otherwise it goes off and keeps its code only if a later step needs it. INCONCLUSIVE gets 3 more reps once, then goes off. For a hitch change (R3-2's upload draw and worker-wait fixes, scored on hitch metrics per R3-2), (i) and (ii) read on its predicted hitch metrics instead: first-turn max and h100 better by a real delta, and no still / moving / tour fps segment worse by one.
decisionRules.implementation: hbreport.py r3_keep (predictions from each arm's `predict`, resolved in the bench dir's own queue item; look gate from `--look ARM=pass|fail`; binding-thread ms = the median over each arm's VALID hbanatomy reps under `--anatomy` (rule V per rep), the move judged real by R1 with its noise from those reps). The hitch-change reading of (i) and (ii) (the sentence added 2026-10-30) is NOT applied by r3_keep: no M1 arm is a hitch change; score one by hand from the first-turn max and h100 rows.

decisionRules.name: look
decisionRules.text: WHAT kernels: bit-exact, or <= 1 f32 ulp, in node or cargo; array layers byte-equal on the 1070 readback. HOW changes: rc-eye stills at 1080p with `skytime=13`, compared by `rc_eye_diff.py`, with particles and sway masked. Default threshold: <= 1% of pixels over 8/255 and <= 0.1% over 32/255; each step may set a tighter one. Every heatmap gets a structural review. Then the batched owner eye test; the owner can veto.

decisionRules.name: routing
decisionRules.text: The binding thread is the largest of main busy per frame, CrGpuMain per present, and GPU ms, at the tier's resolution. If GPU ms >= 0.9 x frame time, GPU levers go first. If CrGpuMain >= main, GL-command levers go first (batching, HUD raster). Otherwise main-thread levers. Never claim fps for a lever on a thread that is not binding; book its ms as headroom.

decisionRules.name: stop
decisionRules.text: A structural lane that delivers < 50% of its predicted ms at stage A stops before stage B and gets a written post-mortem.

decisionRules.name: tier presets
decisionRules.text: A tier preset change ships only if it moves the over-budget thread under its ceiling, or is look-neutral and cheaper. Ultra looks change only with explicit owner OK. This includes `objRadius` and any governor knob.

decisionRules.name: probe gate
decisionRules.text: If the M1 structure-ceiling probe's V1/V2 do not cut main-thread world-render ms and CrGpuMain WEBGL ms by >= 40% against V0 on the 1070, R3-4 and R3-5 are re-scoped before any L-sized build: smaller stage A, or GPU-side levers first under R5.
decisionRules.implementation: hbreport.py ceiling (the probe JSON + `trace-split --marks hbSC:` of its trace).

decisionRules.name: WebGPU
decisionRules.text: Go only on the R3-12 criteria plus the owner's charter amendment.

decisionRules.name: reference clients
decisionRules.text: WebAC, OpenAC and upstream numbers are bounds that say which half of the frame to attack. They are never targets, never a pass/fail gate for a step, and never mixed into B0 comparisons. A reference reading on a different machine or content is quoted with that machine and content.

items.precondition: B0 = the snapshot of the MERGED round-3 phase-A tree: M1-PRE `--check-snapshot` found the =rigs reader (mode parse, window.__occlusionCull.mode, stats.cellsSkipped) in the snapshot's own scene3d/occlusion_cull.js, not merely a url-flags row. Per rep, O-rigs is VALID only if its arm gate held after the settle: window.__occlusionCull.mode === 'rigs' AND stats.cellsSkipped > 0 (interior-cell candidates really went proxy-less). On a snapshot that predates the value the old reader (`!(off|0|false|no)`) reads `rigs` as ON and the arm is silently an A/A; there `mode` is undefined and cellsSkipped absent, so the gate fails: hbbench (and hbanatomy's boot) stops the rep and hbreport rule V marks it INVALID, never averaged and never a loss. The report step MUST pass --queue: with it rule V also marks INVALID an O-rigs rep that did not evaluate exactly this gate true (a rep run from an older copy of this file). gateInfo records the mode and stats either way.

arms.name: O-rigs
arms.gateInfo: window.__occlusionCull ? { mode: window.__occlusionCull.mode ?? null, stats: window.__occlusionCull.stats ?? null } : null

protocolExceptions: Profile: W reuses the persistent C:\Temp\cdpwb-wls profile (its ~1.27 GB OPFS DAT cache); record it in the run JSON. W runs warm against our fresh-profile H arms, so first-turn max and h100 are not compared across W and H.
Window: W and both H arms at the same 1920x1080 window, set before navigating; record innerWidth x innerHeight and devicePixelRatio in every arm (hbbench records them for H).

Sky: WebAC has no sky-time override, so W follows ACE's clock. Record ACE's in-game hour at each W rep and run the H arms at the matching skytime (`hbbench.mjs --skytime <hour>`); if the hour cannot be matched, note the mismatch next to the reading.
Panel: all arms on the same 120 Hz panel, vsync state recorded.
Camera: our still segment uses the chase camera behind the player looking north (stillCam az 180 = camera south of the player, heading 0); WebAC parks with acDebug.setPlayerYaw(0).
